Although it can describe the distance decay of urban land density and the urban expansion processes with higher accuracy, it cannot provide a mechanistic explanation. In contrast, the GMP model is a theoretical model derived based on explicit assumptions, which can reveal the reasons for the inverse-S shaped decay pattern of urban land density and the change of urban compactness from a process perspective. This study provides references for the method selection of fitting urban land density spatial decay and the modeling of urban land-use change.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Analysis of $\text{PM}_{2.5}$ Variation in the Nanjing City Using Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition
abstract: With the continuous process of urbanization in China, in the recent few years, the air pollution in Nanjing city has intensified. The occurrence rate of haze has been increasing year by year, having a negative impact on public health and the ecosystem. Moreover, the issue of poor air quality has been receiving more and more attention from the public. Therefore, a thorough study of the spatial and temporal characteristics of air pollution in Nanjing has great practical significance and a potential for practical application. In this study, inhalable particular matter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{PM}_{2.5})$</tex> was selected as the research object. Based on the hourly data released by 13 air pollution monitoring stations in Nanjing over the past year, we used the ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) and the inverse distance weighted (IDW) interpolation method to analyze the time-scale and the spatial distribution variation characteristics of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{PM}_{2.5}$</tex> in Nanjing. The results show: the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{PM}_{2.5}$</tex> concentration in Nanjing had a quasi-periodic variation of 25–30 days on a daily scale, and 1.6-2 months on a monthly scale; the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{PM}_{2.5}$</tex> concentration air pollution index showed four kinds of variation trends during the period from June 2015 to March 2016, namely, continuously increasing, continuously decreasing, increasing first then decreasing, and decreasing first then increasing. If considering the spatial distribution, the concentrations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{PM}_{2.5}$</tex> in the study area increased from north to south during the period from June to August 2015; while it remained basically the same from September to November 2015 and from January to March 2016, respectively. In addition, the spatial distribution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{PM}_{2.5}$</tex> in the study area showed large discrepancies during the month of December 2015, and in some areas, the air pollution was extremely high.

articleTitle: Characterizing urban expansion pattern to understand urban form dynamics based on Google Earth Engine platform
abstract: Monitoring and analyzing urban spatial pattern and dynamic changes can guide the sustainable urbanization process. Based on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform, random forest algorithm was used to extract the urban built-up area of Changchun in 1990, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, and 2020. Subsequently, the landscape expansion index was used to identify the types of urban expansion and explore the evolutionary process of urban expansion patterns. Results show that: (1) Based on GEE platform, the urban built-up area can be quickly extracted with high accuracy, which is faster and easier to operate than traditional remote sensing image processing methods. (2) The urban expansion mode of the study area in the past 30 years has been a dynamic process from “diffusion” to “aggregation”. The center of gravity of the urban spatial pattern is shifting from the “center” to the “periphery”. The combination of GEE platform, OpenStreetMap, and Landsat imagery can effectively and efficiently map the urban expansion and the dynamic urban forms.

articleTitle: The Postmodernity of WEMAP
abstract: In the transferring process from the modern society to the post-modern society, information is transmitted via WeMedia. WeMap is a kind of maps in the time of We Media that are made by the public whose main purpose is to improve the map expressions to avoid the problems due to the lack of spatial cognitive knowledge, and to focus on the expressions of the map users ’ subjective information. Unlike the traditional maps, WeMap aims to express geographical features and phenomena from multiple perspectives and dimensions. Using the Post-Modernist Philosophy to guide technological research, such as Embodied Cognitive View, Prototype Theory of Category and Decentralism, this paper critically analyzes and reconstructs the spatial cognition, information classifications, and cartographic expressions, and forms a conceptual framework of WeMap with post-modern philosophical characteristics.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Evolution of Habitat Quality Based on Ecological Red Line - A Case of Shiyan-Shenanongjia
abstract: Habitat quality is a reflection of regional biodiversity and ecosystem service value, and plays an important role in the harmonious development of man and nature. However, frequent and large-scale human activities are increasingly threatening the quality of habitats on a global scale. This study uses the Habitat Quality Module of the Integrated Evaluation of Ecosystem Services and Tradeoffs (InVEST) model to evaluate the habitat quality and its spatial characteristics in the Shiyan-Shennongjia region from 2000 to 2020. We further compared and analyzed the effects of ecological red lines on habitat quality in the county-level region. The results show that the habitat degradation degree was less than 0.05, and the overall habitat degradation degree was small. The habitat quality in the study area shows a low-high-low-high spatial pattern from north to south, and low habitat quality was mainly concentrated in the construction land and large arable land areas. In addition, comparing the mean values of the habitat quality in each county excluding the ecological red lines and the regions including the ecological red lines, it was found that the habitat quality in each county decreased significantly after removing the ecological red line area, and the ecological protection red line contributed to the improvement of the overall ecological environment of the county. The results of this study could have theoretical support and policy significance for the maintenance of biodiversity and the protection of the natural environment in the study area.

articleTitle: Targeting the spatial context of risk factors associated with heat-related mortality via multiscale geographically weighted regression
abstract: Extreme heat events appear to be a major cause to weather-related human morality in much of the world. The association between heat stress and public health is recognized as a complex interplay of multifaceted factors. Effective policy-making and action plans require a better knowledge of where and which of those factors should be targeted for intervention. However, little research has separated the underlying scales of effect of key components or taken into account geographical context in an analysis of those factors, which could lead to misguided policy actions in heat health risk reduction. In a case study of Hong Kong, we use the most recent multi-scale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) methodology to narrow this gap. We find that via MGWR, a combination of global and local processes could produce a better fit for the risk of heat-related mortality. Explanatory variables can be divided into three groups: global variables (such as age, educational attainment, and socioeconomic status), intermediate variables that vary on a relatively small scale (such as work environment, place of birth, and language), and local variables (i.e. thermal environment, low income). These findings suggest the need for targeting spatial context to multi-dimensional factors associated with heat-related mortality and highlight the hierarchical policy-making processes and site-specific action plans.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Evolution and Meteorological Drivers of PM2.5 Concentrations in the Yangtze River Delta, China
abstract: China has conducted various measures for air pollution control and promptly alleviated major air environmental problems. However, many severe challenges of air pollution, especially PM2.5 pollution, still exist in China. By using the PM2.5 concentration data during the period of 2015–2018 and meteorological data in 2017 of 227 sites in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD), China, trend analysis, Moran's I, and geographically weighted regression were used to investigate the spatiotemporal pattern of PM2.5 concentrations and the spatial variations of meteorological influences on PM2.5 concentrations in the YRD. Results showed that PM2.5 concentrations in the YRD exhibited an overall decreasing trend, with a growth rate of -3.75 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{g}/(\mathrm{m}^{3}\cdot \mathrm{a})$</tex>. Obvious regional differences were observed in PM2.5 concentrations, and the high-value areas were concentrated in the northwestern YRD and the low-value areas were mainly distributed in the southeastern YRD. The influences of meteorological factors on PM2.5 in the YRD varied in each season. In winter, wind speed and rainfall negatively affected PM2.5 concentrations. By contrast, sea level pressure, relative humidity, planetary boundary layer height, and temperature positively influenced PM2.5 concentrations.

articleTitle: A study on the distribution of 5A attractions and the Spatio-temporal characteristics of tourists' emotions in China
abstract: In-depth exploration of the distribution of attractions and the emotional characteristics of tourists is an important tool to promote tourism in China. Firstly, this paper uses python technology to obtain and pre-process the 5A attraction data of 31 provinces (cities and districts) in China from 2007-to 2021. Secondly, SnowNLP was improved and the sentiment was classified for visitor comments while sentiment values were calculated. Finally, the Spatio-temporal characteristics of the distribution of 5A attractions and tourists' emotions in China are explored in terms of the overall distribution, Spatio-temporal evolution, and Spatio-temporal changes in tourists' emotions respectively. Results show that: (1) China's 5A attractions are spatially characterized by an aggregated distribution, while their degree of aggregation shows a linearly decreasing trend; in time, the total number of 5A attractions rises year by year, and the annual increase shows a decreasing trend year by year. (2) Visitor comments as a whole show a gradual increase with the month, and their sentiment value tends to decrease month by month. (3) Popular attractions are skewed towards the eastern region and negative attractions towards the western region. Knowledge of the development of China's tourism industry and the temporal and spatial changes in tourists' emotions can guide the development of the tourism industry and promote urban-rural integration.

articleTitle: A Coarse-to-Fine Approach for Urban Land Use Mapping Based on Multisource Geospatial Data
abstract: Timely and accurate land use mapping is a long-standing problem, which is critical for effective land and space planning and management. Due to complex and mixed use, it is challenging for accurate land use mapping from widely-used remote sensing images (RSI) directly, especially for high-density cities. To address this issue, in this paper, we propose a coarse-to-fine machine learning-based approach for parcel-level urban land use mapping, integrating multisource geospatial data, including RSI, points-of-interest (POI), and areas-of-interest (AOI) data. Specifically, we first divide the city into built-up and non-built-up regions based on parcels generated from road networks. Then, we adopt different classification strategies for parcels in different regions, and finally combine the classified results into an integrated land use map. The results show that the proposed approach can significantly outperform baseline method that mixes built-up and non-built-up regions, with accuracy increase of 250% and 30% for level-1 and level-2 classification, respectively. In addition, we examine the rarely explored AOI data, which can further boost the level-1 and level-2 classification accuracy by 13% and 14%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and also indicate the usefulness of AOIs for land use mapping, which are valuable for further studies.

articleTitle: A phased vehicles evacuation planning method for disasters with time-dependent traffic demand
abstract: Emergencies such as natural disasters or terrorist attacks seriously threaten the safety of urban residents. The regional centralized development of cities has increased the difficulty of evacuation. In order to avoid traffic congestion caused by large-scale vehicle evacuation, a time-division delayed evacuation planning method is proposed for urban traffic emergency evacuation with disaster warning information in this paper. It makes up for the shortage of existing methods that cannot handle the time-dependent evacuation demand well. Based on the network flow model, the time-division delayed method is used to control the loading time and routes of the evacuation demand by discretizing evacuation demand and optimizing the dynamic origin-destination (OD) demand. In the case study and analysis, the method avoids the traffic congestion caused by the surge of dynamic evacuation demand and improves evacuation efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on the extraction method of impervious surface in Nanjing based on random forest classification
abstract: The distribution of urban impervious surfaces is usually recognized as a significant environmental and an essential indicator of various urban problems. The typical methods of extracting impervious surfaces are Linear Spectral Mixture Analysis Method (LSMA), Exponential Method (EM), and Maximum Likelihood Classification Method (MLC). However, all of the above methods have their drawbacks. Therefore, we propose a new method for extraction of urban impervious surfaces based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Random Forest (RF). The synthetic aperture radar data and hyperspectral data of Nanjing are employed to test and validate the proposed methodology. The result of this new method is compared with the results obtained by LSMA, EM, and MLC to evaluate feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed methodology to extract the urban impervious surface. Experiments show that the Kappa coefficient in the optimal random forest model can reach 0.9744 and the overall classification accuracy is 99.6402%, which has obvious advantages over other methods.

articleTitle: An ORB-SLAM3 Autonomous Positioning and Orientation Approach using 360-degree Panoramic Video
abstract: In order to solve the problem of insufficient support for 360-degree panoramic data in current mainstream monocular visual SLAM system, this paper proposes a highly universal 360-degree panoramic SLAM method on the basis of ORB-SLAM3 system framework. Firstly, considering that SLAM system does not support panoramic video input effectively, source panoramic video is preprocessed into sequential fisheye images with four perspectives. Secondly, a universal fisheye image calibration method based on three dimensional calibration field is proposed to solve the calibration plate dislocation caused by data splicing of panoramic video shots. Finally, ORB-SLAM3 autonomous positioning and orientation of sequence images from different perspectives is carried out, and its accuracy is analyzed and evaluated. Experimental results of indoor and outdoor datasets show that, SLAM localization and pose determination results from different perspectives segmented from the same panoramic video are relatively consistent with high accuracy. In conclusion, the method proposed in this paper can achieve 360-degree panoramic video autonomous positioning and orientation robustly, with a wide application prospect in various artificial intelligence fields, such as unmanned vehicle driving, mapping of unmanned aerial vehicle exploration in unknown areas, robot autonomous positioning and navigation, etc.

articleTitle: Fairness Evaluation of Health Service Facilities Based on Accessibility: A Case Study of the Metropolitan Area of Jinan City
abstract: Health is the most basic pursuit of human beings. People's requirements for health are increasing in modern urban life. The construction and allocation of urban health service facilities have attracted extensive attention from society. It is a significant guarantee to effectively respond to health emergencies and improve the sense of security of urban residents by ensuring the fairness of urban health services. In this study, an improved two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) method was used to evaluate the accessibility to health service facilities in the metropolitan area of Jinan City, and the fairness of health service facilities distribution was evaluated by the Gini coefficient with accessibility as a quantitative index. The results show that the accessibility to the health service facilities of Lixia District and Tianqiao District is higher, and the fairness of the two districts is the strongest, the Gini coefficient of the overall health service is 0.118 and 0.134 respectively, while that of Licheng District is 0.517, which means there is an “obvious gap” in spatial allocation. The overall health service's Gini coefficient of the study area is 0.259, the allocation of health service resources is reasonable. The conclusions and methods of this study can be extended to other study areas as a paradigm, which is of great significance for achieving the equalization of medical services, promoting social equity, and improving the level of urban development.

articleTitle: Study on the spatio-temporal distribution of tourists by coupling questionnaire survey and GPS data
abstract: Studies on tourists' behaviors often require individual background and spatio-temporal information. This study combined a questionnaire survey and GPS data to analyze the visitors of Baiyun Mountain Scenic Area, Guangzhou in terms of their group characteristics, activity patterns, spatial distribution, and influencing factors. Results showed that (1) tourists mostly chose to take the bus/metro (53.06%) to visit the scenic spot, mainly for relaxing and unwinding (59.18%). The largest proportion of tourists visited this place for the first time (56.12%) and the majority was young and middle-aged tourists (86.74%). (2) According to a week-long observation data, the number of visitors was low from hours 1–7, accounting for only 3.9%. The number of visitors increased from hours 8–13, accounting 27.8% of the visitors. The peak was reached during hours 14–19 and receded in the succeeding hours, accounting for 40.1% and 28.3% of all visitors, respectively. (3) Density analysis revealed that the spatial aggregation of tourists in the area overlapped with the attractions, the place where attractions were concentrated was also the area where tourists were densely distributed. (4) Visibility analysis indicated that the size of the viewable area of a hiking trail was correlated with the number of tourists. (5) Lastly, regression analysis revealed that the bus route (0.822) and the distance from the summit park (0.524) had a relatively significant influence on tourists' choice of park entrance.

articleTitle: Water Transparency Inversion Method of Dongting Lake based on Feedforward Neural Network Learning
abstract: Water transparency reflects the nutritive degree of inland lakes. Remote sensing inversion of lake transparency can be used for rapid monitoring of water quality in a large range, which is of great significance for timely management of lakes and protection of aquatic ecological environment. Taking Dongting Lake as an example, based on Landsat 5 remote sensing images, this paper proposes a time-series remote sensing monitoring method of lake transparency based on feedforward neural network learning. This method combines the measured water quality observation points with Landsat 5 remote sensing images, and adopts feedforward neural network to establish a remote sensing inversion model of water transparency. The temporal and spatial distribution of water transparency in Dongting Lake was inversion based on remote sensing images. The results show that it is possible to apply the feedforward neural network learning to the transparency inversion of Dongting Lake. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> between the predicted value and the measured value is 0.638, the root mean square error (RMSE) is 0.048m, and the average relative error is 0.042m. The inversion results can be effectively applied to the water quality analysis and monitoring of the transparency of Dongting Lake.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Feature Selection Approach for Flash Flood Disaster Risk in Jiangxi Province, China
abstract: Appropriate feature selection is critical for flash flood disaster risk assessment as the premise of flash flood warning and forecast. Furthermore, a thorough examination of the algorithm for selecting flash flood risk features and the handing of unbalanced data is required. This study proposes a practical hybrid feature selection approach based on the combination of random forests (RF) and simulated annealing (SA) with a case study in Jiangxi Province, China. By employing weighted samples as the input to the RF-model, this method reduces the influence of unbalanced samples. Results indicate that: The optimal weighting ratios for terrain features are 3:1 or 4:1. The optimal weighting ratios for rainfall features are 2:1 or 3:1. The findings of the two algorithms are combined with physical interpretation of features and concentration time in mountainous catchments, resulting in the selection of four terrain features: slope, maximum elevation, outlet catchment area, confluence time, and four rainfall features: the annual maximum variation coefficients of 10 minutes, 6 hours (CV_M10, CV_H6), and the mean of annual maximum rainstorm of 10 minutes, 6 hours (EX_M10, EX_H6).

articleTitle: Integration and application of spatial information model for earthquake damage assessment based on cloud architecture in Yunnan
abstract: It is critical for governments to immediately assess disaster loss in order to determine key rescue regions, send rescue teams, and other rescue materials following the earthquake. This study presents data resources, a geographical information model, and software system integration in a cloud computing environment to address unresolved difficulties in data, model, software, and service. On May 21,2021, we performed the fast assessment of a magnitude 6.4 earthquake in Yunnan Yangbi using the software system. The real application results reveal that the seismic quick assessment program based on cloud architecture has substantially improved in terms of system stability, model dependability, evaluation efficiency, emergency product diversification, and output result display. It can give basic information support and assurance for earthquake response decision-making.

articleTitle: Extreme Precipitation Susceptibility Map over the Main Mining Areas of China Based on Satellite Precipitation Products
abstract: Extreme precipitation is of vital importance for mining safety, which is also the key issue for ecological treatment of mining areas. Satellite precipitation estimates is a major source of precipitation data, which is the only promising global product with continuous spatiotemporal coverages. However, the potential risk analysis based on Satellite precipitation products in mining areas is almost an unexplored field. This study aims to map an extreme precipitation susceptibility over the main mining areas of China. First, the accuracy of two highly approved satellite-based precipitation products, Global Satellite Mapping of Precipitation (GSMap) and Integrated Multi-Satellite Retrievals for Global Precipitation Measurement (IMERG), are evaluated. Then the spatiotemporal characteristics of extreme precipitation events are explored by analysing the precipitation measures, e.g., the number, mean intensity and duration of extreme precipitation events, over the main mining areas of China during the past two decades. The results demonstrate that, (1) GSMap preforms better in most cases than IMERG in terms of the correlation coefficients (CC∽0.734), BIAS (∽0.396), RMSE (∽6.63), and probability of detection (POD∽0.718), against ground observations, which is employed to depict the susceptibility map for extreme precipitation; (2) the number, mean intensity and duration of extreme precipitation events present significant seasonal and regional differences, where the number and mean intensity are remarkably increasing during the past two decades; and (3) the susceptibility map shows that mining regions over the Kuye River basin and the southeastern study area are relatively more vulnerable to the extreme precipitation events, which should be paid on great considerations during the mining activities. Results of this study indicate that it is more suitable to apply GSMap in mining areas, and provides a novel perspective for the safety mining related fields.

articleTitle: Spatial pattern and factors analysis of farmland in Maonan district
abstract: Taking Maonan district as an example, this paper analyzes its farmland distribution using landscape indices and Geodetector. Studies show that (1) farmland is mainly concentrated in four towns, which are located in the northwest, south and northeast of study area. These towns are core contribution areas of food production, which have over 3/4 farmland areas. (2) After calculating average nearest neighbor index and Moran's I index, it is found that overall layout of farmland presents cluster distribution with “outer high, middle low”. It is mainly because central area is downtown of Maoming city. (3) By calculating landscape index, it is found that Jintang, Aotou, Jintang and Gongguan have high patch density and lower fractal dimension. These towns have simple structures and high regularity which making they becoming core high-quality demonstration areas. (4) It is found that most of patches (88.07%) are small and regular after clustering analysis. The scale and morphological values of cluster centers are 1.96 and 1.11, respectively. The patch distribution patterns like circular, grid, branch and random scattered. (5) By analyzing influencing factors using Geodetector, it is found that the most important factor on patch area and patch shape is distance to residential areas. Among them, natural environmental conditions (elevation, slope and river) are dominant factors for patch area. While main factors for patch differentiation are linear features such as rivers, village roads and main roads.

articleTitle: Study on Landscape Ecological Risk and Its Response to Human Activities in the Lower Yellow River Region, China
abstract: The assessment of the landscape ecological risk reveals the potential harmful ecological effects of ecosystem structure and function on the landscape scale under human intervention, which is significant for the maintenance and protection of regional ecological security. Based on six periods of land use data, this study evaluated the landscape ecological risk and the intensity of human activities in the lower Yellow River region from 1995 to 2020, and analyzed the spatio-temporal evolution characteristics and interrelationship quantitatively. The results show that: (1) The main landscape types in the lower Yellow River region were cultivated land and construction land, in which the area of cultivated land was decreasing and the area of construction land was increasing. (2)Landscape ecological risks are generally dominated by lowest risk levels, and the ecological risk index firstly decreased, then increased and then decreased, and the peak value of the index appears in 2015. (3) The intensity of human activities showed a trend of continuous growth, and the intensity of human activities in the study area showed a trend of transferring from the northwest to the administrative centers of cities. In the areas with high intensity of human activities, the level of ecological risk was higher, and the spatial correlation was the highest; on the contrary, in the areas with low intensity of human activities, the level of ecological risk was lower, and aggregation was not significantly dominant. This study is of considerable referential and practical importance in deepening the understanding of the interference of human activities on ecological risk, defining the ecological risk area and carrying out prevention and control.

articleTitle: Identification of Urban Functional Regions based POI data and the economic contribution index, a case study of Chongqing, China
abstract: Urban Functional Regions is an important basis for analyzing the urban spatial pattern and understanding urbanization progress. Accurately identifying the Urban Functional Regions is conducive to maximizing space efficiency. Point of interest (POI) data is strongly correlated with human activities and the function of urban areas. The identification of urban functional areas only by POI data points is challenging due to the differences in the numbers of different categories of POI data. In this study, we explored the economic contribution index and combined the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and entropy method to modify the functional index model to identify the urban functional zones of Chongqing city, China. Results show that: 1) Single-type functional areas are dominantly distributed in the periphery of the study area. 2) In the dominant functional area, “finance-company” and “factory-company” POIs account for the highest proportion, and the two have a strong homogenization effect, which can better attract employees in spatial agglomeration. Overall, applying POI data and economic contribution index to modify the functional index model provides us with further solutions to urban functional region identification and improves the way of urban system analysis.

articleTitle: Identification and optimization of functional characteristics of territorial space in Anning City
abstract: Based on the perspective of ecological-production-living function, with 2019 as the time section, and based on the land use data and socioeconomic data, the variation coefficient method, TOPSIS model, comparative advantage degree and GIS spatial technology are used to identify the spatial function characteristics of Anning City, optimizing and reconfiguring its development pattern, in order to provide a decision basis for urban function positioning and territorial space development and protection in Anning City. The results show that: (1) The streets with the strongest evaluation of production function in Anning are distributed in the streets in the southern part of the study area and Cao Pu street; the areas with the strongest evaluation of living function are Lian Ran street and Jin Fang street in the central city of Anning; the areas with high evaluation of ecological function are Bajie street and Qing Long street.(2) Forming five functional optimization zones of land space in Anning City and analyzing the characteristics of each functional area and orienting different street development directions with balanced development of land space.

articleTitle: Evolution and Driving Forces of the Landscape Change Pattern of Non-Construction Land in Downtown Chengdu
abstract: We analyzed the dynamic change characteristics of non-construction land undergoing dynamic change and their influencing factors to provide inputs for non-construction land planning. Using land use maps derived from remote sensing image data for downtown Chengdu for the years 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, and 2020, we applied the landscape transfer matrix and binary logistic regression methods in a quantitative analysis of the characteristics of the evolution of the landscape pattern of non-construction land in central Chengdu from 1995 to 2020 and its driving forces. During the period 1995–2020, the area of non-construction land in downtown Chengdu decreased annually, while the area of construction land correspondingly increased, with changes of 20.27% and 20.22% in the respective proportions of both areas, indicating distortion in the strategic position of non-construction land. From 1995 to 2020, the non-construction landscape in central Chengdu changed dramatically, and its evolution was closely related to the urban development status, with the predominant type of landscape change involving cultivated land. From 1995 to 2020, dominant factors influencing the evolution of the landscape pattern of non-construction land were the distance of land from roads and population density. Therefore, a planning system for non-construction land should be developed, and key nodes in non-construction land should be identified to develop more targeted planning policies and maximize the ecological value of non-construction land.

articleTitle: Distribution Characteristics and Image Perception Differences of Urban and Rural Tourist Attractions: A Case of Beijing
abstract: Under the background of urban-rural integration development, how to promote the coordinated development of urban-rural tourism has become a research hotspot. In order to excavate the cultural connotation of scenic spots, cultivate the growth point of characteristic tourism, strengthen the interaction between urban and rural tourism, and realize the goal of win-win regional tourism. This paper takes 209 popular tourist attractions in Beijing as the research object, crawls the scenic spot POI and comment text data from the Ctrip travel network, and uses text mining and spatial statistical analysis to explore the spatial distribution characteristics and image perception differences of urban and rural tourist attractions. The results show that: 1) Tourist attractions in Beijing have obvious spatial agglomeration characteristics, and the agglomeration degree of urban attractions is higher than that of rural attractions. 2) The overall image perception of Beijing tourist attractions is positive, and the network attention and emotional values of urban attractions are generally higher than those of rural attractions. 3) The network attention pattern of urban scenic spots is basically consistent with the emotional spatial distribution pattern of scenic spots, and the network attention pattern of rural scenic spots is significantly different from the emotional spatial distribution pattern of scenic spots. Research shows that there are great differences in spatial distribution characteristics and image perception between urban and rural tourist attractions in Beijing. Analyzing the natural and humanistic factors behind the differences can provide effective guidance for the coordinated development of urban and rural tourism.
